identifying the signal sequences that are recognized by the SRP pathway, and we have identified a number of new signal sequences that are exported in a SRP-dependent manner.

SRP-dependent signal peptides are those that promote efficient export of thioredoxins.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrophobic core of a signal sequence, as well as the amino acid sequence of the mature protein, are important factors that contribute to the mechanism of export.
a signal sequence that promotes export by an SRP-dependent mechanism is likely to export a rapidly folding protein.
SRP-dependent signal peptides are those that promote efficient export of thioredoxins, while non-SRP-dependent signal peptides are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SRP pathway is not a passive mechanism that simply transports a protein to the membrane; rather, it is a mechanism for the export of a subset of proteins that have evolved to utilize this pathway.
thioredoxin can be used as a reporter to identify SRP-dependent export.
the SRP pathway can be used to export proteins that would not be exported by the posttranslational pathway.
